title: 1.6 Accuracy and Estimation

icans: I can estimate results with an appropriate level of accuracy.
I can decide how many items I need and round correctly in context.
I can choose an appropriate approximation for a measurement.

vocab: how close a measured or ____________ value is to the actual value
when you need __________ (bags, buses, cans), always round up

blocks.p: Mulch: a 12 ft by 8 ft garden bed, 3 inches deep. Bags hold 2 ft³ or 2.5 ft³.
Paint: 980 ft² of fence. One gallon covers 350 ft².

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Round up: When you need enough of something, always round _______________.

blocks.stem: A sandbox is 6 feet by 5 feet and 1.5 feet deep. Sand comes in bags of 0.8 cubic foot. How many bags do you need?

notes: Accuracy: A measurement can be only as accurate as the _______________ used to measure it.
Final answers: Round a final answer to a _______________ level of accuracy for the situation.

blocks.stem: A student says the hallway is 152.387 meters long. Is that an appropriate measurement? What would be better?
